sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- A.C.Srivastava,Subham Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
152 of 2023 at Police Station-Loni Border, District-Ghaziabad under Sections 304B, 498A IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The applicant is in jail since 06.06.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 27.06.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri A.C. Srivastava, learned counsel assisted by Shri Shubham Singh, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Ms.
Sujata Chaudhary, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
Prakesh vs State Of U.P. on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3681061/
1 1.
The applicant is the husband of the deceased.
2. The applicant never demanded dowry or harassed the deceased.
3. The applicant is bereaved by the death of her wife.
4. The deceased was a temperamental lady who was prone to extreme reactions over trivial issues.
5. On the fateful day, after a some arguments in the household, she flew into a fit of rage and took the extreme step of ending her life.
She committed suicide by hanging.
6. The postmortem report opines the cause of death as asphyxia due to antemortem hanging.

7. Injuries depicted in the postmortem report consistent with hanging are:
(i). Nature of ligature marks.
(ii).
No abnormality was detected in the hyoid bone.
8. The applicant did not abet or instigate the deceased to commit suicide.
9. The prerequisites for attracting the presumptions under Section 304B IPC are not made out in the facts and circumstances and evidence of the case.
10. Prosecution evidence does not connect the applicant with the offence.
11. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
12. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of her influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Prakesh be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.
The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
( i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.

Prakesh vs State Of U.P. on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3681061/
2
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
